 Judgment
[Maca Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021] This order of this Court shall dispose of two motor accident
claims appeals, one preferred by the insurance company and the another by the claimants against
the award da
ted 18.3.2020 in OP(MV) No.119/2018 of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tirur.

2. The facts, in brief, are as follows:
On 12.2.2017 while late Mr.Rijo Jose was riding a motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-48-A-3141 from Wadakkenchery-Kunnamkulam road, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-48/H-9878 driven in a rash and negligent manner came and hit the motorcycle of the deceased Rijo Jose.
As a result of the accident, the deceased fell down to the road and sustained fatal injuries.
He was taken to Aswini Hospital, Thrissur and on the way to the hospital he succumbed to the injuries.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged 42 years and was self-employed doing business in furniture, rice and flour mill and tourist vehicle hiring.
He was also the Chairman of Nithya Sahaya Kuries Pvt. Ltd. and was earning a monthly income of Rs.1,25,000/-.

The wife, two minor children, the father, and the mother of the 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 deceased Rijo Jose approached the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tirur, seeking compensation for the loss of the deceased.
On behalf of the claimants, Exts.A1 to A23 were produced and marked.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced on the side of the insurance company.

The tribunal took notice of Ext.A22 series of income tax return verification forms and assessed the gross income of the deceased as one reflected from the income tax return for the year 2016-17 and proceeded to fix the yearly income of the deceased at Rs.3,77,186/- and proceeded to calculate the compensation for loss of dependency.
While doing so, the tribunal did not accept the claim of claimants 4 & 5, who are the parents of the deceased.

Thus, the Tribunal granted the following compensation:

sentences.text: Heard Sri.George Cherian, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company in MACA No.115/2021 assisted by Smt.Latha Susan Cherian and Sri.P.V.Chandramohan, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants.

5. Sri.George Cherian, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company primarily contended that the income fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.3,77,186/- per annum is highly exorbitant.

He would point out that the legal heirs of the deceased had continued the business and therefore, had not sustained any loss of earnings, and the Tribunal ought to have considered the subsequent earnings of the family of the deceased while computing the income for the loss of dependency.

6. On the other hand, Sri.P.V.Chandramohan, the learned 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 counsel appearing for the claimants controverted the submissions of Sri.George Cherian contending that the Tribunal while calculating the income for the purpose of assessing loss of dependency is not expected to travel beyond the relevant pleadings and assess the subsequent earnings or loss that is caused in the family business, which was run by the deceased.
If the proposition, as canvassed by the learned Senior Counsel, is accepted, according to the learned counsel for the claimants, it will lead to an incongruous situation.

In support of his contention, he relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Malarvizhi v.
United Insurance Company Ltd. [2020 (1) KLT 511 (SC)].

He further pointed out that under no stretch of imagination, the Tribunal could have excluded the claimants 4 &
5 from the purview of the dependency compensation.
Therefore, he prayed that the appeal by the claimants be allowed and a suitable enhancement be granted.

sentences.text: I have considered the rival submissions raised across the bar.

8. Before proceeding to consider the question as to whether the claimants are entitled to enhancement in the compensation, it is 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 pertinent to consider the contention raised by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the insurance company.
The decision to be taken by this Court in the appeal preferred by the Insurance Company will ultimately depend upon the chance of the claimants to seek appropriate enhancement in the compensation.

9. The prime contention of the learned Senior Counsel on behalf of the Insurance Company is that while calculating the income, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the prospective income that was generated out of the business carried on by the family of the deceased.
At first blush, it may appear that the contention raised on behalf of the learned Senior Counsel is appealing.
However, on a detailed analysis of the aforesaid contention, this Court is of the considered view that the contention is not only untenable but against all notions of law.
Loss of dependency is calculated based on the income that was generated by the deceased at the time of the accident.
This forms an integral part of the multiplicand for the purpose of calculating loss of dependency.
It is thereafter that an appropriate multiplier is applied.

Accepting the argument of the learned Senior Counsel would lead to a situation where while calculating the component of the 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 multiplicand, the Tribunal will be required to assess the future income of the family concerned, which was run by the deceased.
This, in turn, would convert the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 into an adversarial litigation, which is impermissible in law.
The concept of the grant of compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is generally just and fair compensation.

If the argument of the insurance company is accepted, it will lead to a situation where the Tribunal will have to traverse outside the concept of just and fair compensation enshrined under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
In the present case, Ext.A22 series of income tax returns show that the deceased was having a reasonably good annual income.
It is immaterial as to whether the said annual income would increase or decrease subsequent to the accident.
Therefore, this Court has no hesitation in its mind to hold that the argument raised by the learned Senior Counsel on behalf of the insurance company is untenable.

10. Having found that the argument as regards the calculation of the income for the purpose of ascertaining the multiplicand is untenable, this Court now proceeds to consider the 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 question as to what should be the income of the deceased.
It is beyond doubt that Ext.A22 series stood unequivocally proved before the Tribunal.
For the assessment year 2014-15, the income of the deceased was Rs.4,00,560/-, and for the years 2015-16 and 2016-17, it was Rs.4,68,034/- and Rs.3,82,218/-, respectively.
11. A reading of the aforesaid three returns would show that there was a substantial increase in the annual returns for the year 2015-16, whereas there was a reduction for the year 2016-17.
However, it is pertinent to note that the returns for the year 2016-17 was filed on 9.2.2017, whereas it ought to have been filed after 31.3.2017.
The reason which prompted the deceased Rijo Jose to file income tax return before the due date is immaterial.

Admittedly, the income tax return shows that the return The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Divya Rijo Jos @ Divya on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106787603/
6 was for a period of ten months.

sentences.text: Therefore, the question would be whether the same could be construed as the basis for calculation of the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose.

Pertinently,
the Tribunal has not taken this amount as the annual income, but, in fact, reduced the same and fixed it at Rs.3,77,186/-.

Sri .P.V.Chandramohan, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants,
submitted that the deceased Rijo Jose 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 had filed the income tax returns well before due date and therefore the last return is required to be taken for the purpose of arriving at his income.
This Court finds considerable force in the contention of the learned Counsel for the appellants.

A close scrutiny of the income tax return for the year 2016-17,
shows that deceased Rijo Jose paid Rs.3,82,218/- as income for 10 months and thus calculating the average income for the year it comes to Rs.4,58,661.60 (38,221.8 x12).

On a comparative assessment of the three income tax returns, the incidental question before this Court would be as to which return should be taken by this Court for the purpose of calculating the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose.
It must be remembered that the grant of compensation under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 should be just and fair.
No doubt, the statute is a beneficial legislation and therefore requires to be construed liberally.
As against three income tax returns, can this Court take the returns which show more income?.

The answer perhaps lies in the decision of the Supreme Court in Malarvizhi (supra).
12.
In Malarvizhi (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court was considering the sustainability of the view taken by the High Court 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 while computing the multiplicand.
On facts of the case before the Supreme Court, there were three income tax returns for the assessment years 1997-1998, 1999-2000 and 2000-2001.

The High Court while considering the claim for enhancement, took the income tax return for the assessment year 1997-98 being the highest one and not the subsequent income tax return, which showed a considerable reduction in the annual income.
Though it was urged before the Supreme Court that income from other sources will have to be reckoned along with the income as reflected in the income tax return, the same was not accepted.
Be that as it may, the Apex Court accepted the methodology adopted by the High Court by taking the income tax return which was highest at the relevant point.

13. Applying the same principle to the facts of the case, this Court is of the considered view that among Ext.A22 series, the income tax return for the year 2015-16 could be taken for the purpose of calculating compensation towards loss of dependency.
Thus, an amount of Rs.4,68,034/-is fixed as the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose.

14. Moving forward, the further question to be considered by 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 this Court is regarding the findings rendered by the Tribunal that claimants 4 & 5 are not dependent on late Rijo Jose.
The finding cannot be sustained for the reasons to follow.

In Kirti v.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. [(2021) 2 SCC 166], the Hon'ble Supreme Court considered the claim for dependency of a mother-in- law on account of death of her son-in-law.

entities.text:
Kirti v.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. [(2021) 2 SCC 166]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held by the Supreme Court that for claiming compensation under the head loss of dependency, there need not be any direct financial dependency of the claimants towards the deceased.

Even when a mother-in-law is considered to be dependent upon the deceased since it was shown that they were residing together and she was fully dependent upon her son-in-law for the purpose of livelihood, one cannot fathom the reasoning of the Tribunal as how the claimants 4 & 5 being the father and mother The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Divya Rijo Jos @ Divya on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106787603/
7 of the deceased Rijo Jose, could be excluded.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Divya Rijo Jos @ Divya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, to that extent, the said finding of the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.
15. As an upshot of the aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered view that the appeal preferred by the Insurance Company is liable to be dismissed.
Insofar as the appeal preferred by the claimants is concerned, the claimants are entitled to succeed.

The 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 compensation granted by the Tribunal towards loss of dependency has to be necessarily modified by refixing the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose at Rs.4,68,034/-.
Since the deceased was aged 42 at the time of death, the claimants are entitled to have future prospects reckoned at 25%.

By taking an amount of Rs.4,68,034/- towards the annual income, the monthly income of the deceased Rijo Jose is fixed at Rs.39,000/- and adding 25% future prospects,
the income would be Rs.48,750/-.

Hence, the additional compensation towards loss of dependency and the other heads under which the appellants are entitled to enhanced compensation is calculated as under :

 add 25% future  prospects  48,750)
2

The claimants are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.12,36,429 (Rupees Twelve lakhs thirty six thousand four twenty nine only) over and above the compensation granted by the The Oriental Insurance Co. sentences.text: They are entitled to interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization with proportionate costs on the enhanced compensation.
The Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation together with interest and proportionate costs within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
In the result, MACA No.456/2024 filed by the claimants is allowed and MACA No.115/2021 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
No order as to costs.

This forms an integral part of the multiplicand for the purpose of calculating loss of dependency.
It is thereafter that an appropriate multiplier is applied.
The concept of the grant of compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is generally just and fair compensation.
If the argument of the insurance company is accepted, it will lead to a situation where the Tribunal will have to traverse outside the concept of just and fair compensation enshrined under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
In the present case, Ext.A22 series of income tax returns show that the deceased was having a reasonably good annual income.
It is immaterial as to whether the said annual income would increase or decrease subsequent to the accident.
11. A reading of the aforesaid three returns would show that there was a substantial increase in the annual returns for the year 2015-16, whereas there was a reduction for the year 2016-17.
On a comparative assessment of the three income tax returns, the incidental question before this Court would be as to which return should be taken by this Court for the purpose of calculating the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose.
It must be remembered that the grant of compensation under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 should be just and fair.
No doubt, the statute is a beneficial legislation and therefore requires to be construed liberally.
13. Applying the same principle to the facts of the case, this Court is of the considered view that among Ext.A22 series, the income tax return for the year 2015-16 could be taken for the purpose of calculating compensation towards loss of dependency.
Thus, an amount of Rs.4,68,034/-is fixed as the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose.
In Kirti v.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. [(2021) 2 SCC 166], the Hon'ble Supreme Court considered the claim for dependency of a mother-in- law on account of death of her son-in-law.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Insofar as the appeal preferred by the claimants is concerned, the claimants are entitled to succeed.
The 2024:KER:94382 MACA Nos.115/2021 & 456/2021 compensation granted by the Tribunal towards loss of dependency has to be necessarily modified by refixing the annual income of the deceased Rijo Jose at Rs.4,68,034/-.
Since the deceased was aged 42 at the time of death, the claimants are entitled to have future prospects reckoned at 25%.
By taking an amount of Rs.4,68,034/- towards the annual income, the monthly income of the deceased Rijo Jose is fixed at Rs.39,000/- and adding 25% future prospects,
the income would be Rs.48,750/-.
Hence, the additional compensation towards loss of dependency and the other heads under which the appellants are entitled to enhanced compensation is calculated as under :

6 . Pain and suffering 15,000 16,500-15,000=

 Total 12,36,429/-

The claimants are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.12,36,429 (Rupees Twelve lakhs thirty six thousand four twenty nine only) over and above the compensation granted by the The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Divya Rijo Jos @ Divya on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106787603/
8 Tribunal.
They are entitled to interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization with proportionate costs on the enhanced compensation.
The Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation together with interest and proportionate costs within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
In the result, MACA No.456/2024 filed by the claimants is allowed and MACA No.115/2021 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
